attributes.detection_recipe: For every declaring TU of a flagged symbol, grep its access sites (not just the declaration). Classify each site: (a) PASS-THROUGH -- the symbol is only ever passed as a function argument or explicitly cast to another pointer type before any arithmetic (`(T*)symbol`, `f(symbol)`) -- the declared element type never reaches codegen, so any type disagreement here is cosmetic; (b) SELF-CONSISTENT SCALED ARITHMETIC -- the TU does `symbol + N` / `symbol[N]` where N is chosen assuming the TU's OWN declared element size (byte offset if u8[], element count if f32[]/f64[]), and N*sizeof(declared_type) independently resolves to the SAME target byte offset that every other declaring TU's own scaled arithmetic reaches (cross-check via a canonical struct layout elsewhere, e.g. `gdlmem.py struct`, or by comparing the resolved byte offsets algebraically across all declaring TUs). Both (a) and (b) are BENIGN: no live codegen bug exists, and 'fixing' a (b)-class declaration by simply retyping it to match a sibling TU is actively DANGEROUS -- it silently rescales every `+N`/`[N]` site written for the old element size, introducing a real addressing bug where none existed. Only case (c) -- a genuine scalar READ/WRITE/ASSIGNMENT whose target asm shows an actual narrowing/behavior difference at that exact site (the fctiwz/stfd/lwz/stw tell, or two TUs' scaled arithmetic algebraically reaching DIFFERENT byte offsets) -- warrants a declaration fix. Procedure: `grep -n "<symbol>" <each declaring TU>.c` (usage, not just decl), classify every hit, and only escalate to fnasm/fndiff verification for (c)-class hits.
attributes.provenance: 2026-08-30 whole-tree externcheck.py sweep (work_claim.extern-conflict-fix.20260830.v1): 6 of externcheck's 7 flagged float/int-class conflicts turned out to be entirely or partially (b)/(a)-class once every declaring TU's access sites were read, not just its declaration line. Verified benign pairs/sets (no fix made, none needed): gCameras (src/game/world/gauntworld.c:4153,6174 declares u8 but every access is `((f32*)gCameras)[75/76/77]` or `*(f32*)(gCameras+300/304/308)` -- the explicit cast/byte-offset neutralizes the array's own declared type); gFloorCollisionResult (src/game/enemy/critter.c:346 u8 uses `gFloorCollisionResult+0x34`/`+0x44` byte offsets; src/game/game/pmotion.c:248 f32 uses `gFloorCollisionResult[13]` float-index (13*4=0x34) plus explicit `(u8*)gFloorCollisionResult+0x44` casts for the other field -- both independently reach worldcol.c's canonical FloorCollisionResult.floorY@0x34 and .current@0x44); lbl_8023CA98 (critter.c f32 `+4` elements, enemy.c f32[][4] `[1]` row, pmotion.c u8 `+16`/`[0x10]` bytes, sfx.c u8 `+16` bytes -- ALL FOUR independently resolve to the same normal-vector field at byte 0x10, confirmed via pmotion.c's own comment 'normal @+0x10'); lbl_802C2A28 (mb_tree.c u8 manual `+idx*16` byte stride, pb_objregs.c f32[256] `[idx*4]` element index -- both reach the same 16-byte-stride table entry, confirmed via pb_objregs.c's own `(u32)&lbl_802C2A28[idx]` address-only usage); lbl_80127D40 (bosscam.c u8, but its ONLY uses are `YawVec3(lbl_80127D40, ...)` against a local `void* axis` parameter -- pure pass-through, pattern (a)). Separately, a PASS-THROUGH-only conflict IS still worth normalizing for documentation/latent-bug-prevention even though it produces zero measured byte movement: gIdentityMatrix (11 TUs: anim.c, combat.c/InitCamera, gamemain.c, mb_objects.c, mb_poly.c, psfx.c, sys/main.c, ui/attract.c, ui/auxscreen.c, world/worldcol.c) and lbl_80127D00 (sys/main.c) were retyped from u8/s32/char to f32 with a full-ninja-green, byte-for-byte-identical project progress report (97.83% fuzzy / 58.15% matched / 2602/2990 functions unchanged to the byte) -- confirming pattern (a)'s prediction that pass-through-only sites carry zero codegen risk either way. One EXCEPTION found while doing this: src/game/mb/mb_blit.c ALSO pass-through-uses gIdentityMatrix, but that TU independently mis-prototypes the callee (`extern void* MBNewNode(int a, const char* name, int b);` vs the real `MBNewNode(MBTreeNode*, const f32*, s32)` defined in mb_tree.c) -- retyping gIdentityMatrix there broke compilation (`cannot convert 'const float *' to 'const char *'`) because the SECOND, unrelated, function-prototype conflict (out of extern-DATA-symbol scope) was masking/absorbing the first; reverted that one file, left both bugs coexisting and undocumented-but-inert.
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies whenever tools/gdl/externcheck.py (or an equivalent whole-tree extern-decl census) flags a symbol as float/int-class conflicting -- read every declaring TU's ACCESS sites before assuming the census output alone indicates a live bug or a safe fix.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: An externcheck-flagged float/int-class extern-type conflict does NOT by itself indicate a live codegen bug. It is benign when every declaring TU's usage is either (a) pure pointer pass-through (cast or passed as an argument before any arithmetic -- the declared element type never affects codegen) or (b) self-consistent scaled arithmetic (`symbol + N` / `symbol[N]` where N is chosen assuming that TU's OWN declared element size, and independently resolves to the SAME target byte offset every other declaring TU's own scaled arithmetic reaches). Only a genuine scalar assignment/comparison with a target-asm-visible narrowing tell (fctiwz/stfd/lwz/stw replacing a target's single stfs/lfs -- see claim.law.cross-tu-extern-type-mismatch-fctiwz-tell), or two TUs' scaled arithmetic algebraically landing on DIFFERENT byte offsets, is an actual bug worth fixing. Retyping a (b)-class declaration to match a sibling TU without checking its own arithmetic is actively dangerous: it silently rescales that TU's `+N`/`[N]` sites (written for its old element size) and introduces a genuine addressing bug where none existed. (a)-class conflicts are safe-but-usually-inert to normalize (zero measured byte movement in every verified instance) except where a SEPARATE, unrelated declaration bug in the same TU (e.g. a mismatched function prototype for the callee the symbol is passed to) is coincidentally absorbing/masking the data-symbol conflict -- check the TU still compiles after the edit, don't assume pass-through is risk-free. Verified 2026-08-30 across gCameras, gFloorCollisionResult, lbl_8023CA98, lbl_802C2A28, lbl_80127D40 (all benign, no fix made or needed) and gIdentityMatrix/lbl_80127D00 (pass-through, normalized in 11+1 TUs, byte-identical full-ninja result) -- of externcheck's 7 flagged conflicts that day, exactly one component (sys/main.c's lbl_80127D00) was a genuinely wrong-but-harmless declaration whose fix fully eliminated that symbol from the census; the rest were either already-correct-elsewhere pass-through normalizations or provably benign self-consistent arithmetic requiring no change.
